alerts.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 18 at 10:11PM CDT by NWS Brownsville TX
alerts.description:
The combination of hot temperatures and humidity will produce heat
index values between 108 and 111 degrees for several hours
Sunday afternoon and early evening. A few locations may briefly
experience heat index values above 111 degrees.

If spending time outside on Sunday, drink plenty of water, wear
light weight and light colored clothing, and take frequent breaks
from the heat. Young children and pets should never be left
unattended in vehicles.

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued July 18 at 8:15PM CDT until July 22 at 12:23AM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
alerts.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

San Antonio River At Goliad affecting Calhoun, Goliad, Victoria and
Refugio Counties.

For the San Antonio River...including Goliad...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...San Antonio River at Goliad.

* WHEN...From Sunday afternoon to late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...At 25.0 feet, Minor lowland flooding occurs, with water
in the lowest areas of Goliad State Park. Livestock below Goliad to
the Guadalupe River confluence are cut off and potentially drown.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:00 PM CDT Saturday the stage was 19.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 22.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage early
tomorrow afternoon to a crest of 27.0 feet Monday morning. It
will then fall below flood stage Tuesday morning.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued July 18 at 8:35PM CDT until July 20 at 4:09PM CDT by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX
alerts.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

San Antonio River at Hwy 72 near Runge affecting Goliad and
Karnes Counties.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...San Antonio River at Hwy 72 near Runge.

* WHEN...Until Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 31.0 feet, Flooding spreads across the wide flood
plain upstream and downstream. No structures are threatened.
Livestock and farm equipment will need to removed from the
floodplain.
At 39.0 feet, Water is well into the floodplain. No impacts to
roads or structures. Cattle and farm equipment should have been
removed from the floodplain or face the threat of being cut off or
lost.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 PM CDT Saturday the stage was 33.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 22.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours
ending at 8:15 PM CDT Saturday was 33.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 34.5
feet just after midnight tonight. It will then fall below
flood stage early Monday morning.
- Flood stage is 27.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of
35.9 feet on 04/08/2023.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued July 18 at 4:30PM CDT until July 22 at 12:26PM CDT by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX
alerts.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Asherton affecting Dimmit County.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Asherton.

* WHEN...Until early Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 31.0 feet, The Nueces River and Turkey Creek are a
mile and a half wide south and west of Crystal City. Farm to
Market 190 is flooded over a mile near the Nueces River and the
bridge floor is flooded. Livestock should be moved from the flood
plain. Upstream, Highway 85 becomes impassable as routed water
spills into Soldier Slough and over the highway.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 3:30 PM CDT Saturday the stage was 31.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 18.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours
ending at 3:30 PM CDT Saturday was 31.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 31.5
feet this evening. It will then fall below flood stage early
Wednesday morning.
- Flood stage is 20.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of
30.9 feet on 10/06/1959 or about a foot higher than the 30.21
on July 4th 2002.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 18 at 10:56PM CDT until July 19 at 1:00AM CDT by NWS San Angelo TX
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southern Fisher County in west central Texas...
Central Nolan County in west central Texas...

* WHEN...Until 100 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1054 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 2 inches are expected over the
area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Sweetwater, Maryneal, Longworth, Camp Boothe Oaks, Gannon, Busby
and Capitola.
- This includes Interstate 20 between Mile Markers 239 and 254.

This includes the following Low Water Crossings...
IH 20 frontage roads crossing Plum Creek, IH 20 frontage roads,
Bitter Creek crossing Bitter Creek, County Road 180 crossing Oak
Creek, County Road 180 crossing Bear Creek and County Road 181
crossing Robertson Creek.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 18 at 10:46PM MDT until July 19 at 2:45AM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Arroyo and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...A portion of western Texas, including the following
county, Hudspeth.

* WHEN...Until 245 AM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Runoff in normally dry arroyos. Dangerous flows over
low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1046 PM MDT, Widespread showers with embedded heavier
thunderstorms have been affecting rural southern Hudspeth
County. This will likely result in inundated arroyos and low
water crossings across that area through tonight. Quitman
Canyon and arroyos crossing FM-192 just south of Fort Quitman
have received over an inch of rain. Other areas around Indian
Hot Springs Road will also be impacted.
- Some locations that may experience flooding include...
Indian Hot Springs, Fort Quitman, Frenchman Canyon,
Esperanza, Indio Mountains Research Station, Bosque Bonita
and Quitman Canyon.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
